izzyondroid:de.buttercookie.simbadroid.name: SimbaDroid
izzyondroid:de.buttercookie.simbadroid.summary: A simple SMB file server (needs root)
izzyondroid:de.buttercookie.simbadroid.description:
SimbaDroid is an SMB server for Android, allowing you to access the contents of your storage (both internal storage or an external SD card) from your computer via wi-fi.
 Due to Android limitations, this app requires root (as on all Unixoid operating systems, it is not possible to open a port < 1024 otherwise, and the default SMB port is 445 and Windows doesn't work with anything else). Without root, you either need some sort of SMB client which allows configuring the port used (SimbaDroid uses port 4450 behind the scenes), or some kind of port mapping software to allow Windows to transparently connect to port 4450.
 Due to JFileServer limitations, only SMBv1 is supported, which isn't ideal for modern Windows, either, but c'est la vie…
 Since the app is mostly for my private use, at the moment there are no configuration options – shares for the internal storage as well as an external SD card (if one is detected) are set up automatically and are accessible without authentication, so be careful about using this app in public networks. I might add some options for configuring your own custom shares and user authentication eventually, but no guarantees as to if and when.
 READ/WRITE/MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is required for filesystem access.

fdroid:dk.cocode.parvaz.name: Parvaz
fdroid:dk.cocode.parvaz.summary: Farsi-first browser tunnel through a self-hosted Apps Script relay
fdroid:dk.cocode.parvaz.description:
Parvaz (Persian for "flight") is a Farsi-first Android app for Iranian users that tunnels browser traffic through a Google Apps Script relay deployed and controlled by a trusted technical helper.
The app terminates TLS locally using a certificate the user installs once, then re-encapsulates HTTPS requests inside the relay's JSON protocol and forwards them through Google's infrastructure. Chrome and other Chromium-based browsers (Brave, Edge, Vivaldi) trust this certificate automatically; native apps, non-Chromium browsers, and non-HTTP protocols are out of scope by Android design.
Because the relay operator can read all tunneled traffic in plaintext, Parvaz is intended for read-only browsing of public information rather than signing in to sensitive accounts, unless the user fully trusts the operator running the relay.
Setup requires installing a certificate through Android Settings once and importing a parvaz:// access link shared by the helper. After that, one tap starts or stops the tunnel from the main screen.
Throughput is limited by the underlying Apps Script quota, and WebSockets are not supported.

fdroid:invalid.lena.scrcpy.name: scrcpy
fdroid:invalid.lena.scrcpy.summary: Mirror a second Android device over wireless ADB. No root required.
fdroid:invalid.lena.scrcpy.description:
This app mirrors a second Android device on your phone or tablet over Wireless
ADB, the same way the desktop scrcpy tool does.
The device running this app is the source; the target is any Android 11+ device
with Wireless Debugging enabled. Video, audio, touch, key input, and clipboard
are forwarded between them. No root is required on either side.
Features:
* Wireless pairing and connection using the target's Wireless Debugging code
* Live video mirroring with selectable codec (H.264, H.265, or AV1)
* Audio forwarding with selectable codec (raw or Opus)
* Multi-touch, soft keys, and two-way clipboard sync
* Adjustable max size and bit rate
* Automatic reconnection when the link drops
The app pushes the scrcpy server, built from Genymobile's scrcpy sources, to the
target device and speaks the scrcpy protocol directly. It is written in plain
Java with no proprietary dependencies.
This is an independent client. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or
produced by the scrcpy project or Genymobile; "scrcpy" is used only to say
which protocol it speaks.
Connections require TLS. Android's Wireless ADB protocol authenticates the
client to the target, but its target certificate is process-scoped and cannot
be pinned as a stable target identity. Use a trusted private network. To reach
a remote target, put both devices on a VPN such as WireGuard rather than
exposing the target's wireless-debugging port to the internet.

fdroid:io.keepalive.lite.android.name: Keep Alive Lite
fdroid:io.keepalive.lite.android.summary: Notify others if you haven't used your device in a given period of time
fdroid:io.keepalive.lite.android.description:
Keep Alive will send a custom message via SMS to one or more people if you haven't used your device in a given period of time. Intended to be used as a failsafe for those living alone in case of an accident or other emergency. Once the settings are configured, no further interaction is required.
- 100% Device-based, no cloud services or accounts required
- Free with no ads or trackers
- Open Source (https://github.com/keepalivedev/KeepAlive)
- Minimal Battery Usage
- Multiple SMS Recipients
- Custom Alert Message
- Optional: Include Location Information in SMS
- Optional: Place a phone call with speakerphone enabled
- Optional: Send an HTTP request to a custom URL
Requirements
 Keep Alive requires that your device has an active cellular plan. WiFi calling and messaging will be used if the device supports it.
How it Works
 Keep Alive uses either your device's lock screen or another app(s) to detect activity. If your device hasn't been lock or unlocked for a set period of time, or if you haven't accessed the selected app(s), you will be prompted with an 'Are you there?' notification. If this notification is not acknowledged an Alert will be triggered. Based on the configured Emergency Contact Settings, one or more SMS messages and/or a phone call will be placed to notify others that you may be in need of assistance.
WARNING: If your device restarts, Keep Alive will not be able to check for recent activity until the screen is unlocked. On Android 7.0+, Keep Alive can still send an alert before the screen is unlocked but must assume you have been inactive based on its last saved state. On older Android versions, Keep Alive cannot run at all until the screen is unlocked and alerts will not be sent.
Main Settings
- Monitoring Method - Choose between using the lock screen or another app(s) to detect activity. If using another app(s), you will be prompted to select the app(s) to monitor.
- Hours of Inactivity Before Prompt - how many hours since your phone was last locked or unlocked before you are prompted with an 'Are you there?' notification. Defaults to 12 hours
- Minutes to Wait - if the prompt is not acknowledged within this time, an Alert will be sent based on the configured emergency contact settings. Defaults to 60 minutes
- Rest Period Time Range - a range of time during which inactivity will not be counted. For example, with 'Hours of Inactivity' set at 6 hours and a Rest Period of 22:00 – 6:00, if the device is last used at 18:00, the 'Are you there?' check would not be sent until 8:00. Note that an alert can still be sent during a rest period if the 'Are you there?' check was sent BEFORE the start of a rest period.
- Auto-Restart Monitoring After Alert - If enabled, monitoring will be automatically restarted after an Alert is sent.
- Alert Webhook - Configure an HTTP request to be sent when an Alert is triggered
Emergency Contact Settings
- Phone Call Number (Optional) - when an Alert is triggered a phone call will be placed to this number with speakerphone enabled
One or more SMS recipients can be configured with:
- Phone Number - the phone number to send the Alert SMS to
- Alert Message - the message that will be sent when an Alert is triggered
- Include Location - if enabled, your location will be included in a second SMS
Privacy/Data Collection
No data is collected other than the configured settings and nothing is shared with the developers or any 3rd parties. The only data transmitted is to the configured emergency contacts.
Disclaimer
- Not responsible for SMS or phone call charges incurred by the use of the Keep Alive app
- The operation of the Keep Alive app is dependent on the device, software, and network connectivity. The developers are not responsible for any failure due to device malfunctions, software incompatibilities, or network issues.

fdroid:website.sung.mangossh.name: MangoSSH
fdroid:website.sung.mangossh.summary: Secure SSH and Mosh client with encrypted profiles and backups
fdroid:website.sung.mangossh.description:
MangoSSH is a free and open-source SSH and Mosh client for Android phones and tablets. Profiles and keys stay in an encrypted vault, and encrypted backups can live on your own WebDAV server.
Sessions:
* SSH and native Mosh terminals; Mosh keeps an authenticated SSH companion for files, port forwards, and server resource reports
* Jump hosts, SSH agent forwarding, and optional tmux workspaces that reattach on reconnect
* Snippets that run automatically when a shell opens
* Live connection health and sessions that stay up in the background
Authentication and security:
* Password, private-key, and keyboard-interactive authentication with one-time password prompts
* Explicit host-key confirmation and a clear warning when a saved key changes
* Generate, import, and export RSA, ECDSA, and Ed25519 keys
* Encrypted local vault for profiles, keys, and host fingerprints
* App lock with PIN or biometrics and a configurable auto-lock delay
Files and forwarding:
* SFTP browser with file and folder upload and download
* Pause, resume, and retry transfers, and continue them after reconnecting to the same verified host
* Edit small text files in place with a diff preview and encrypted drafts
* Local, remote, and SOCKS5 port forwarding, with or without an open terminal
Networking:
* Per-profile route: direct, the system Tailscale VPN, or an embedded, outbound-only Tailscale node (tsnet)
Terminal:
* Cascadia Mono PL, JetBrains Mono NL, and Fira Code fonts
* Mango Dark, Dracula, Nord, and Solarized themes, or custom colors
* Configurable shortcut bar, scrollback, pinch-to-zoom, and immersive mode
Backup and more:
* Encrypted file and WebDAV backups with a preview before merging, recovery points, and remote history
* Import hosts from an OpenSSH config file
* English and Simplified Chinese; two-pane layout on tablets
Mosh is rebuilt from the included GPL-licensed source for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86, and x86_64. Embedded Tailscale is opt-in, does not request Android VPN access, and requires the user to authorize their own Tailnet account, on Tailscale or on a self-hosted control server such as Headscale.
MangoSSH does not include advertisements or analytics. Credentials, private keys, host fingerprints, OTP answers, and session keys are never included in diagnostics.

apple-itunes:6797273528.description:
SIGLINK keeps your group talking when the network doesn't.
Nearby iPhones and iPads running SIGLINK connect directly over peer-to-peer Wi-Fi and Bluetooth: no cell tower, no router, no SIM, no internet. It even works in airplane mode with Wi-Fi switched on. Every device also passes messages on for the others, so a message can hop across a crowd, a campsite or a building to reach someone well out of direct range. Whenever any device has internet, messages also travel through the SIGLINK relay, and wait there for anyone whose app is closed until they're back.
END-TO-END ENCRYPTED
Every message, photo, voice note and group update is sealed on your device for each recipient. Relaying devices and our servers carry it without being able to read it. Scan a contact's code in person to verify their key; if a key ever changes, SIGLINK tells you.
NEW: AN AI ASSISTANT THAT WORKS OFFLINE
Ask by voice or text, in your own language, with no internet: where your team is and who has gone quiet, a note in another language, the numbers for a climb. It runs entirely on your device. Your voice is recognised on the device, and answers are read aloud by Eve, a natural English voice that also works offline. Four models to choose from:
- Apple Intelligence: built in, on iPhone 15 Pro and later with iOS 26
- LFM3 1.7B, Fast: quick answers about your map, beacons and chats. iPhone 11 and later (not iPhone SE 2nd generation)
- Qwen3.5 4B, Writer: writing and translation in many languages. iPhone 15 Pro and later
- Nemotron 3 Nano 4B, Analyst: numbers and step-by-step reasoning. iPhone 15 Pro and later
Each model downloads once, then works offline. Online, it can look things up when you ask. Your Apple Watch can ask too, and reads the answer aloud.
ON APPLE WATCH
- Push to talk to your group or one person; their voice messages play as they arrive
- Read your chats and reply by dictation, scribble or a voice message
- A map of your team and beacons, and who has gone quiet
- Complications for unread messages, who's in range, your GPS position and Talk
- Works through your iPhone, or on its own over Wi-Fi or cellular
WHEN THE NETWORK FAILS
- Festivals, stadiums and events where the network is jammed
- Hiking, climbing, camping and the backcountry
- Field teams, crews and volunteers coordinating on the ground
- Ships, planes, tunnels and remote sites
- Power cuts and outages
FEATURES
- 1:1 and group chats, with search and filters for unread, favorites and groups
- Hold-to-talk voice messages, and a Walkie-Talkie mode that plays them aloud as they arrive
- Voice and video calls, directly with people nearby or over the internet; add people to a call
- A Calls tab with favorites and recents; missed calls reach all your devices
- Photo sharing, compressed to travel the mesh, with location data removed
- Add people by scanning their SIGLINK code, or invite them with a link
- Sent, delivered and read ticks, typing indicators and reactions
- Notifications for new messages, even with the app closed
- Radar: your contacts on a satellite map, only if they choose to share, with offline maps
- Intercom: a chat between your own iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch
- One identity across your devices, and an optional encrypted backup
- Block and report anyone from a chat
EXTENDED REACH
The standard mesh carries a message across up to 64 relaying devices. A one-time Extended Reach purchase raises that to 255, for very large crowds and spread-out teams.
PRIVATE BY DESIGN
Sign in once with an email address; no phone number or SIM. Your address book is never uploaded. After that, SIGLINK works with no connection at all. Location sharing is off until you turn it on. Chat history stays on your devices and out of iCloud backups.
Direct range between two devices is typically 30 to 100 metres, depending on surroundings; each SIGLINK device in between extends it.

• Pick your look: a clean stylised globe with crisp country borders and a latitude/longitude grid, or a realistic Earth. Both look great in Light and Dark Mode.
PIN YOUR PLACES
Build your own travel record, as simple or as detailed as you like.
• Tap "Edit Places" to add, edit, or remove places.
• Tap "+" to add a place: drop a pin on the map and the city and country are filled in for you, or type them in yourself.
• Add the date of your visit and your own notes.
• Attach up to 12 photos to each place. They appear above the globe whenever you visit that place; tap one to see it full screen and zoom in.
• Keep a wish list: turn on "On my wish list" and the places you dream of get pins in a color of their own.
FIND PLACES IN YOUR PHOTOS
Pin the Globe looks at where and when your photos were taken, and groups your geotagged pictures into suggested places for you to review.
• Each suggestion shows the place's name, when you were there, and a preview of your pictures.
• Add a suggestion with a single tap and its photos come along, or open it in the editor to fine-tune it first.
• Leave out your everyday area, around home and work, so only your trips show up.
• Only look at photos taken after a date you choose, so a new scan picks up where the last one left off.
• Access to your photo library is only requested when you open Find in Photos.
TRACK YOUR PROGRESS
See how far you've come: the number of places, countries, and continents you've visited, with a breakdown by continent and by country. Every country and every continent counts. Even the ones with just one pin are a reason to plan your next trip. Your wish list also shows how many new countries and continents are still waiting for you.
SHARE YOUR WORLD
• Record a movie of one full revolution of your globe, then share it with friends or save it to Photos (iPhone and iPad).
• Send your places to another device with AirDrop, Messages, or Files. When you open them, choose whether to replace your places or merge them in.
• Your photos stay with you: they are never included in a shared file.
MAKE IT YOURS
• Load 200 demo places to see what a well-traveled globe looks like, and remove them when you're ready to start your own. Demo places never count toward the free limit.
• Wipe everything and start fresh at any time.
MADE FOR iPHONE, iPAD, AND MAC
Pin the Globe adapts to every screen and window size. On iPad and Mac the place editor opens in a side panel next to the globe, so you can watch your pins appear as you add them. On Mac, browse a place's photos with the arrow keys.
FREE TO TRY
Pin the Globe is free to try with up to 30 places. When you reach the limit, you can keep using every feature with your 30 places, or unlock unlimited places with Pin the Globe Unlimited, a one-time purchase. No subscriptions. No ads. No account needed.
Bought Pin the Globe before it became free? Unlimited places are already yours.

flathub:games.zetsubou.MaxMassacre.description:
Max Massacre is a fantasy visual novel with a single choice to determine the ending.
 In a world filled with monsters, demons, and other inhuman creatures, mankind is no longer the dominant race. 
 Humans are nothing more than cattle, fed on by more powerful entities and hunted down for sport. 
 Humans in general are weak, not even a match for the children of those who hunt them, and they know it. 
 The human race is steadily declining, and before long, mankind will exist no longer.
 As a child born into such a world, Max aspires to become a hero. A mighty warrior who will save the human race from the cusp of extinction, 
 wielding strength unheard of for a boy on the brink of adulthood. He is already the strongest fighter in his village in hand to hand combat, 
 and he has killed his fair share of low-level monsters. At seventeen years of age, he is well on his way to becoming the hero he aspires to be, 
 and no matter how much his fellow villagers hate and scorn him for his demonic aura, Max wishes to save every one of them.
 Forever by Max's side is his childhood friend and love interest, Celeste. Like Max, she possesses incredible strength, and is by far the strongest 
 sorceress in the village. She is knowledgeable, intelligent, well-liked, and quite attractive; a truly fortunate young woman in almost every way imaginable. 
 However, beneath this amiable exterior is a mind far more cynical and unforgiving. She does not share Max's outlook on life, nor does she condone his desire 
 to become a hero, or to protect those who harm him. To her, humans are no better than the demons oppressing them, and she would happily leave their 
 village in flames, if only Max would go with her.
 As Max and Celeste go about their routine lives in the small village they call home, their differing views on the world clash every day, 
 with each one trying to convince the other to see the light. But with the other villagers all living in fear and contempt of Max, 
 and not hesitating for a moment to show how they feel, Celeste has a clear advantage. She believes it's only a matter of time before 
 Max realizes what a fool he has been, and with the level of malice being directed towards Max increasing day by day, she might be right.
 Will Max manage to convince Celeste that the human race is worth protecting? Or will Celeste prove to Max once and for all that 
 his enemy is not demonkind, but the familiar faces of those who deny his humanity?

fedora-packages:bidscoin/bidscoin.description: BIDScoin is a user-friendly Python application suite that converts (“coins”) source-level (raw) neuroimaging data sets to standardized data sets that are organized according to the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) specification. Rather than depending on complex programmatic logic for source data-type identification, BIDScoin uses a mapping approach to discover the different source data types in your repository and convert them into BIDS data types. Different runs of source data are uniquely identified by their file system properties (e.g. file name or size) and by their attributes (e.g. ProtocolName from the DICOM header). Mapping information can be pre-specified (e.g. per site), allowing BIDScoin to make intelligent first suggestions on how to classify and convert the data. While this command-line procedure exploits all information available on disk, BIDScoin offers a Graphical User Interface (GUI) for researchers to check and edit these mappings – bringing in the missing knowledge that often exists in their heads only. This interactive step can also be skipped for employment in fully automated dataflow pipelines. BIDScoin requires no programming knowledge in order to use it, but users can use regular expressions and plug-ins to further enhance BIDScoin’s power and flexibility, and readily handle a wide variety of source data types.

firefox-addons:3068519.name: Timebox-productivity
firefox-addons:3068519.summary: A light-weight, no non-sense productivity extension which enables the persistent or scheduled blocking of distracting websites to aid users in staying focused.
firefox-addons:3068519.description:
TIMEBOX 
Stop losing your afternoon to "just checking" those distracting sites.
 Focus, on your terms. 
Timebox is a focus tool that blocks distracting websites the way YOU work - not with a rigid, one-size-fits-all list you can't touch. Pick how a session starts, decide exactly what's off-limits, save your favorite setups, and even schedule it all to run itself. No accounts, no cloud, no tracking - everything stays on your own device.
 HOW YOU FOCUS IS UP TO YOU 
 Manual mode : block everything until you personally turn it back off.
 Timed sessions : pick 25, 45, 60, or 90 minutes and it stops on its own.
 Pomodoro mode : 25 minutes locked in, 5 minutes free, repeating for as long as you like.
Three ways to start a session, zero ways to accidentally leave it blocking forever.
 BLOCK WHAT ACTUALLY DISTRACTS YOU 
Organize sites into groups - Social Media, News, Shopping, and Adult content come built in - and flip an entire category on or off with one switch. Add your own sites to any group, or leave them ungrouped with their own individual toggle. It's your list, arranged your way, not a fixed blocklist someone else decided on. Moreover, Timebox automatically catches regional variations of sites you want to block without you having to hunt each one down.
 ONE CLICK, HOWEVER YOU LEFT IT 
Set up your ideal "Work" configuration once - which groups are on, which are off - and save it as a Profile. Switching between deep-focus mode and a lighter setup is one click, not five minutes of re-toggling.
 SET IT AND FORGET IT 
Schedule sessions to start automatically on the days and times you already know you need to focus - no need to remember to hit start every single morning.
 NEED FIVE MINUTES? TAKE THEM 
Hit snooze for a short window — 1, 3, 5, or 10 minutes — when you genuinely need to check one thing without ending your whole session. Blocking resumes automatically, and your timer or schedule keeps running the whole time underneath. No guilt, no having to remember to turn it back on yourself.
 PEACE OF MIND FOR SHARED DEVICES 
Need to keep a shared computer - or a child's browsing - off-limits during certain hours? Set a password and lock the browser completely. Every open tab is safely tucked away and reopens automatically the moment it's unlocked, and a built-in auto-unlock timer means nobody can ever get permanently locked out. Lock it manually whenever you need to, or schedule it to lock itself, every day, on its own.
 SEE WHAT FOCUS ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE 
Timebox quietly keeps score: how many times it's caught you before a distraction, how long you've genuinely focused, how many sessions you've completed — plus a simple 7-day trend so you can see the pattern build. It never records which sites you tried to visit or when, just the counts. Motivation without the surveillance.
 BUILT FOR PRIVACY 
Timebox doesn't ask for an account, doesn't phone home, and doesn't track what you do. Every setting, every blocked site, every schedule, and every stat lives in your browser's own local storage — full stop. Even the usage stats are built to keep as little as possible: counts only, nothing about which sites you visited, with old daily data automatically aged out rather than kept forever.
Timebox is aimed for anyone who is looking for a simple and easy to use tool for improving their focus. This includes:
 Students who need a distraction-free study session
 Remote workers protecting their deep-work time
 Anyone who's opened one "quick" tab and lost the whole afternoon
 Parents managing screen time on a shared or child's browser
Take back your attention. Install Timebox and decide, for once, what your browser is actually allowed to show you.
 FEATURES 
• Manual, timed, and Pomodoro focus sessions
• Snooze blocking for a few minutes without ending your session - your timer keeps running
• Custom groups with one-click enable/disable, plus built-in Social Media, News, Shopping, and Adult categories
• Individual ungrouped sites with their own toggle
• Blocking a site automatically covers its other country-code domains too (e.g. bbc.com also blocks bbc.co.uk )
• Save and reapply named Profiles for different focus setups
• Schedule sessions to start automatically by day and time
• Optional password lock for the whole browser, with automatic tab restore on unlock
• Configurable auto-unlock safety timer - never locked out for good
• Lock scheduling for shared or child devices
• Local usage stats - blocks stopped, time focused, sessions completed, 7-day trend - with no history of which sites or when
• Clean, dedicated screen when a blocked site is visited - no dead ends
• 100% local: no accounts, no analytics, no data collection

firefox-addons:966222.description:
ATTENTION : I'm looking for people's input to help improve this. Details below.
See my video about Link Tools .
A WebExtension that allows you to manipulate links in various ways. Has the following features:
 Get parts of links and altered links, e.g. convert between desktop and mobile links, extract identifiers, or change to alternate domains.
 Operations to copy things to the clipboard and to visit links.
 Can operate on links in the page (right-click) and the page address.
 Can decode embedded links (provided a pattern is known), exposing them to all copy and visit operations.
 Limited ability to decode query parameters.
 Optional popup thumbnails on mouseover (requires URLs that can be derived directly from given links).
 A facility is provided for adding your own operations, as well as importing and exporting them.
Source code is on GitHub . Bug reports and feature requests may be submitted there.
I'm looking for people's input about what types of addresses they'd like to see useful operations on in this extension. Right now, the set of built-ins is quite limited, because that's all I could think of. Although you are able to configure your own, there are probably many that should be included with the extension. If you have ideas, I encourage you to get in touch. You can email me using the support email or website shown on this extension's listing page . If you prefer to chat, you can also try the Discord I set up. Whichever method you choose, try to provide the following in your suggestion:
 A link to the site, if possible. However, if an account is required to access the part of the site where the relevant type of link can be found, unless I already happen to have an account, this will not be helpful.
 One or more examples of such addresses. Remember that Link Tools can only extract information from the address itself; it does not try to look up anything.
 If there are thumbnails associated with such an address, it will help if you can describe or provide examples of those as well. For these, too, it must be possible to generate the address based only on the link. For example, YouTube videos have thumbnails, the addresses of which are generated based solely on the video ID, which is present in the video address; therefore, the thumbnail can be shown when mousing over a YouTube video link.
Another thing that I'm looking for is types of addresses with embedded links. Right now, I only have a handful. I might come up with more myself, but I can't think of everything, so please don't hesitate to submit examples. Thanks.
